# The attribution funnel that collects every touchpoint

A single purchase this quarter can usually be traced back through several earlier touchpoints: a social ad seen three weeks ago, a search two weeks ago, an abandoned cart a week ago, and finally the email that prompted the completed order. Each of those touchpoints happens on a different platform, at a different time, through a different channel entirely, and on its own tells the analytics team almost nothing useful about what actually drove the sale.

The attribution system exists to collect that scattered, diffuse trail of separate touchpoints and funnel all of it down into a single measurable event: one attributed sale, credited in some agreed proportion back to the touchpoints that preceded it. Without that funnel, the marketing team would be looking at a dozen disconnected signals with no way to compare their relative value; with it, every campaign's contribution becomes a single number the team can actually rank against every other campaign's number, which is the entire reason the system was built in the first place.
